title: A lisse locus for a constructible sheaf
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-field, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, with constructible and lisse as in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. There is an open subscheme $U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $F|_U$ is lisse and, if $X\ne\varnothing$, then $\dim(X\setminus U)<\dim X$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $X=\varnothing$, take $U=X$.

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, take $U=X$. The empty family is an etale covering of the empty scheme, so local constancy is vacuous, and there are no geometric stalks to check for finiteness. Thus the restriction is lisse by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. No strict dimension comparison is asserted in this case. Henceforth assume $X\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Empty-space dimension convention; the lisse condition is vacuous on the empty scheme

proof.text: The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: it is a one-point affine scheme and $k$ has only the ideals $0$ and $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the finite-type structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to conclude that $X$ is Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $\kundim X<\infty$. The definition [def-kun-dimension] identifies $\kundim X$ with the supremum of lengths of strict chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $|X|$, which is exactly $\dim X$ in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Thus $\dim X<\infty$. Since $X$ is nonempty, the closure of any point provides a length-zero irreducible closed chain. The chain definition [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] therefore shows that $\dim X=d$ for an integer $d\ge0$.

source.place: Finite type over a Noetherian base; finite dimension is the cited lem-kun-dimension-finite-type

proof.text: Choose the finite partition by locally closed constructible subschemes witnessing constructibility in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. On each stratum the restriction is lisse, hence locally constant with finite stalks as a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules. These same strata and immersions give a stratification [def-constructible-stratification]: they are finitely many pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets covering $X$, with their given immersions. No condition on closures of strata is required. This is the stratification used by [def-constructible-constructible]. The finite-values formulation and the finite-stalk formulation on each stratum agree by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], applied with the same finite ring $\Lambda$. Thus $F$, with coefficient category the category of $\Lambda$-modules throughout, satisfies the constructibility hypothesis of [def-constructible-constructible].

source.place: Finite partition characterization, with module coefficients as in Tag 03RW(3); no change of coefficient category

proof.text: Apply [prop-constructible-generic-constancy] to this constructible sheaf in the coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules. It gives a dense open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ on which $F|_U$ is finite locally constant. By [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] this is precisely the required lisse condition. Only generic constancy is taken from the cited proposition: it is not being used for any dimension assertion.

Put $Z=X\setminus U$ with its subspace topology. It is closed since $U$ is open. It is nowhere dense: its closure is itself, and a nonempty open subset contained in $Z$ would be disjoint from the dense set $U$, a contradiction. We have checked $X$ nonempty, locally Noetherian, and of finite dimension $d$. Apply [lem-sc-hilbert-nowhere-dense-dimension-drop] to this $Z$ to obtain $\dim Z<d=\dim X$, with dimension understood as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. This includes $Z=\varnothing$, whose dimension is $-\infty$. Together with the preceding step this gives both required clauses for the same $U$.
